title: Princeton Summer Journalism Program
description: Free, year-long college-prep and journalism program for high-achieving US high school juniors from limited-income backgrounds. Summer component is a hybrid multi-week intensive: online college-admissions and journalism workshops in June and July, culminating in a 10-day residential experience on Princeton's campus in late July/early August (tours of NYT/CNN/Bloomberg, producing The Princeton Summer Journal).
cost: Free — all costs for the residential portion (travel, housing, meals, equipment) covered by the program
residency_restrictions: Permanent US address; must intend to attend college in the US
selectivity_evidence: Limited to students from limited-income backgrounds; minimum unweighted GPA equivalent to 3.5/4.0; requires teacher recommendation, transcript, and a writing sample. Exact acceptance rate not published on the official page.
verification_status: Verified - official program page fetched (rendered browser, past a Cloudflare check) and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21. Eligibility specifics beyond what that page stated are corroborated by WebSearch of the program's own /apply/eligibility subpage, not independently re-fetched this session.

title: MIT Women's Technology Program (WTP)
description: Four-week summer engineering-intro program at MIT for female-identifying rising high school seniors with strong math/science coursework but little to no prior engineering background — hands-on classes, labs, and team-based projects.
cost: Free to apply; free to attend for families earning under $120,000/year
residency_restrictions: Must live in the US year-round
selectivity_evidence: Selective, holistic review of transcripts/scores/references; no published acceptance rate.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21.

title: Summer@Brown (Pre-College Programs)
description: Brown's pre-college program, 300+ 1-6 week courses spanning humanities, sciences, arts, business, law, and engineering, offered on-campus residential, on-campus commuter, online, and hybrid. Also includes distinct sub-programs (BELL environmental labs, Leadership Institute, STEM for rising 9th/10th graders).
cost: $100 application fee; per-course/format program costs vary widely, not itemized on this page
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21.
researcher_notes: Rolling-style admission (decisions within ~15 business days), not overtly competitive by published evidence -- selectivity_evidence deliberately left null rather than asserting a tier the page doesn't support.

title: Berkeley Pre-College Scholars — Summer Residential Track
description: Residential summer program where high schoolers live on the UC Berkeley campus and take two Berkeley Summer Sessions undergraduate courses (numbered 1-99) for real college credit, plus college-prep workshops and Bay Area excursions.
cost: $15,987 (Session C, 8 weeks, June 22-Aug 14) or $14,687 (Session D, 6 weeks, July 6-Aug 14); includes tuition, housing, meals, insurance
selectivity_evidence: Minimum 3.0 GPA required; not otherwise described as competitive beyond that bar and capacity.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21.

title: University of Toronto Pre-University Program (incl. DEEP Summer Academy)
description: 3-week Advanced Academic Program (AAP) for international high schoolers with advanced English, immersed in Canadian university-style coursework; the Faculty of Applied Science & Engineering's DEEP Summer Academy is a related STEM-focused track for high-achieving students.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21.
researcher_notes: Exact dates/cost not published on this specific page (referred to a separate 'Dates and Fees' page not independently fetched this session) -- left null rather than guessed.

title: MEF University High School Summer School
description: Istanbul-based summer program (20th year running) offering advanced physics and engineering coursework (Advanced Mechanics, Advanced Electromagnetism, Quantum Mechanics, Phase Transitions and Renormalization Group) plus social sciences/architecture/law sessions, aimed at high-achieving Turkish high school students.
selectivity_evidence: Marketed toward outstanding achievers ('Üstün Başarılılara'); cites 12 alumni admitted to MIT's RSI program over the past 10 years and placements at MIT/Harvard/Stanford/Yale/Oxford, though no explicit acceptance rate is published.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21 (content in Turkish, translated).
researcher_notes: Two 2-week sessions (June 29-July 10 and July 13-24); start_date/end_date above span the full range across both.

title: Kadir Has University AI High School Summer Academy
description: 5-day interdisciplinary AI program covering technical AI literacy, autonomous-systems law, AI policy and society, philosophy of intelligence, and future-city design, taught hybrid at KHAS's Cibali campus in Istanbul.
cost: Free — funded by Kadir Has Foundation sponsorship
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read directly by researcher on 2026-08-21.
researcher_notes: Landed on the wrong Kadir Has program on the first attempt this session -- khas.edu.tr/en/summer-school/ is the regular undergraduate/graduate summer-session credit-recovery program for currently-enrolled KHAS students, not this high-school program; caught by reading the actual page content (eligibility talks about 'current Kadir Has University students' and ECTS credits) before publishing it under the wrong identity, same class of trap this campaign's own notes describe for other universities (e.g. Aarhus Master's page, Dublin City University's application-system mismatch). Correct URL found via the announcement page's own outbound link.
